stance_summary: USD legs hide the real AU-CA split: AUDCAD is a 5y extreme while AUDUSD and USDCAD are only mid-70s 1y. HOLD the existing short AUDCAD; do not re-open a duplicate. The cross isolates Australian housing/restrictive-policy risk versus Canada's remaining-hike and energy-pass-through path without Fed contamination.

trade.horizon: 1-3 months through the next RBA/BoC and housing/energy prints
trade.invalidation: The Australian housing channel reverses while AONIA keeps delivering the remaining ~50bp, BoC energy-pass-through risk is withdrawn and CORRA hikes are priced out, and AUDCAD holds the packet 5y extreme instead of mean-reverting. A fresh USD-only shock that moves AUDUSD and USDCAD together without compressing the cross is not the intended falsifier.
trade.thesis: FACT: As of 2026-09-18 AUDCAD spot is 0.9975768872320596, 1y percentile 99.80 and 5y percentile 99.96, with +1.95% 1m and +1.37% 3m; 20d realized vol is 4.38. AUDUSD is only 76.4 1y / 84.3 5y and USDCAD 74.0 1y / 87.0 5y, so the extreme lives in the product of two moderate USD legs, not in either dollar pair. Overnight AONIA is 4.35 with Oct +21.5bp and Mar-27 +51bp (implied 4.86); CORRA is 2.29 with Dec 1m +29bp and Mar-27 +84bp (implied 3.13). AU 2Y is 4.999 at the 99th percentile 1y/5y; CA 2Y is 3.27 at 97.8 1y but only 58.5 5y; CA-AU 2Y is -164.9bp at the 10.5th 5y percentile. AU temperature: inflation 82, labor 50, activity 54, consumer 48. CA: inflation 55, labor 38, activity 66, consumer 45. NSW stamp-duty receipts fell 24% y/y in August with transactions -18% and Sydney/Melbourne values more than 7% below peak. Canada August CPI held at 3% with core near 2%; BoC minutes flag energy pass-through. The book already owns short AUDCAD pos-00661cabb94a, 50m notional, 500k standard-shock risk, mark equal to packet mid. INFERENCE: the market is pricing an RBA-over-BoC currency premium as if Australia can keep tightening from 4.35 into an already-open housing channel while Canada remains a cheap overnight and a cheap CAD in the cross. That is backwards on the remaining path: AONIA has less unused hike room into deteriorating housing, CORRA still prices a catch-up cycle, and energy pass-through is a CAD-specific catalyst. Short AUDCAD owns that differential without a Fed/USD residual. USD expressions (short AUDUSD or long USDCAD) contaminate a clean AU-versus-CA view with the just-delivered Fed 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% and with SOFR 3.85. AUDNZD is also a 5y extreme but NZ official yields and the NZ policy path are unavailable in this packet, so it is not a cleaner cross. Carry opposes the short (AONIA 4.35 versus CORRA 2.29), which is why the book HOLDs 50m rather than ADDs. UNKNOWN: NZ rates, CME FX futures positioning, broker executable quotes, and any labeled historical analog with quantified forward outcomes.
trade.mispricing: AUDCAD at a packet 5y extreme prices a durable Australian yield/policy premium versus Canada even as the AU housing channel is already biting and AONIA still has ~50bp of extra tightening in the strip, while CORRA from 2.29 still prices +84bp by Mar-27 and BoC minutes keep energy pass-through on the table. The USD legs are not similarly extreme, so the mispricing is the cross, not AUDUSD or USDCAD.

expression_comparison.rates_candidate: Receive AONIA_2027-03 (implied 4.86, +51bp vs overnight 4.35) versus pay CORRA_2027-03 (implied 3.13, +84bp vs overnight 2.29), i.e. long AU duration / short CA duration as a rates expression of AU overtightening versus CA catch-up. Packet CA-AU 2Y is already -164.9bp.
expression_comparison.spot_candidate: Short AUDCAD spot (existing pos-00661cabb94a); rejected USD alternatives short AUDUSD or long USDCAD, and rejected AUDNZD because NZ rates are unavailable.
expression_comparison.rationale: Dedicated spot-FX seat. The intended discrepancy is an AU-versus-CA remaining-policy and growth-channel gap. AUDCAD isolates that gap: both AONIA and CORRA paths are live in the packet, both sovereign curves are live, and the 5y FX percentile is 99.96. AUDUSD and USDCAD only mid-70s 1y percentiles, so a USD expression mixes in the already-delivered Fed 25bp hike and SOFR 3.85. The rates RV (receive AONIA / pay CORRA) points the same way but lives in two policy strips that are already pricing the catch-up (CA) and residual hikes (AU); the stretched tradable price is the cross, not a new 2Y CA-AU extreme that still needs a USD residual to mark. AUDNZD is equally extreme but NZ official yields and NZ policy path are unavailable, so it fails closed as a cleaner cross.

context_build.causal_mechanism: Test whether Australia can sustain a near-parity AUDCAD premium when the RBA's tightening channel is already open in housing while the remaining AONIA hike path is still ~50bp, versus Canada still operating from CORRA 2.29 with +84bp priced by Mar-27 and BoC minutes flagging energy pass-through into a 3% headline / ~2% core CPI mix. If AU housing deterioration caps further RBA delivery and CA still has unused tightening plus an energy tail, AUD should cheapen versus CAD. That is an AU-CA relative-policy and relative-growth mechanism, not a USD dollar-bloc mechanism.
context_build.path_to_current_price: Multi-horizon packet path for AUDCAD as of 2026-09-18: +0.20% 1d, +0.36% 5d, +1.95% 1m, +1.37% 3m, into 99.80 1y / 99.96 5y percentiles at 0.99758. The USD legs that compose it did not make the same trip: AUDUSD is +0.09% 1d, -0.73% 5d, +0.20% 1m, +2.65% 3m at 76.4/84.3 percentiles; USDCAD is +0.11% 1d, +1.10% 5d, +1.74% 1m, -1.25% 3m at 74.0/87.0. Information over the same window: Fed 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% and August US CPI keeping a tightening bias; RBA channel showing up as NSW stamp-duty and home-value declines; BoC minutes on energy pass-through and Canada August CPI 3%; two-way oil (Saudi Oman STS workaround versus weakening energy shock absorbers); last-24 desk thesis that energy is constraining global easing. The cross drifted to a 5y extreme while USD pairs stayed only moderately high.
context_build.known_vs_new_information: Known: RBA and BoC have been in a global tightening/energy regime; AU yields were already high; Fed hike was >90% priced into 16 Sep. New enough to move the cross now: the housing channel is in hard receipts (stamp duty -24%, volumes -18%, values >7% off peak), which is transmission of known tightness rather than a new RBA decision; BoC energy-pass-through minutes plus a still-low CORRA overnight versus a still-rich AUDCAD level. Known information explains a new move only if the market had not yet treated the housing print as a cap on remaining AONIA hikes relative to Canada's unused path. The cross at a 5y high says it has not.
context_build.market_implied_assumption: Current AUDCAD requires that Australia keep a policy and yield premium over Canada that justifies near-parity in the cross: AONIA can still add ~50bp from 4.35 without the housing channel stopping the RBA, and CAD does not need to reprice the leftover CORRA catch-up or energy pass-through. It also requires that compounding two mid-70s USD-leg percentiles into a 5y-extreme cross is a fair AU-CA relative price rather than USD contamination.
context_build.market_assumption_disagreed_with: Disagree that the remaining RBA path is more currency-supportive than the remaining BoC path. The housing channel is already biting in Australia while Canada still has the larger unused hike stack from a 2.29 overnight and an explicit energy-pass-through risk. The priced assumption that AUD should sit at a 5y extreme versus CAD is the exact error.
context_build.price_decomposition: Level: AUDCAD 0.99758 is a 5y extreme; change: the 1m +1.95% is the marginal stretch. Decomposition of the cross into packet legs: AUDUSD (not extreme, 5d actually down) times USDCAD (1m up 1.75% but only 74th 1y). The 1m AUDCAD rally is therefore mostly CAD weakness versus USD plus a stable-to-firm AUD versus USD, not an AUD breakout. Rates decomposition: AU 2Y 4.999 versus CA 2Y 3.27 (spread -165bp, 10.5th 5y percentile of CA-AU) already encodes a huge AU yield premium; policy-path decomposition is the better marginal driver — AONIA Mar-27 +51bp versus CORRA Mar-27 +84bp from a 206bp overnight gap (4.35 vs 2.29). The FX has not cheapened AUD for the housing-open / CA-catch-up mix; it has done the opposite.
